entry.title: Bitcoin Core v30.4 Released
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core version v30.4 introduces a range of enhancements and fixes aimed at improving the software’s performance, stability, and usability. The update is available for download at [https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.4/](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-30.4/). This release addresses various bugs, optimizes underlying processes, and incorporates updated translations to support an increasingly diverse user base. Users are encouraged to report any discovered issues through the official GitHub issue tracker at [https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues).
Comprehensive upgrade instructions are provided for users of previous versions. The recommended process involves shutting down the current instance completely before proceeding with installation on Windows or copying the appropriate files on macOS and Linux systems. Upgrading from End-of-Life (EOL) versions is supported, though migration of the data directory may increase upgrade time. Backward compatibility for older wallet versions is generally maintained, ensuring continuity for long-term users.
The software maintains robust compatibility across major operating systems, including Linux Kernel 3.17+, macOS 13+, and Windows 10+. While Bitcoin Core is expected to function on other Unix-like systems, these platforms do not undergo regular testing, and usage on unsupported systems is discouraged to avoid unforeseen issues.
Among the notable changes, the software now complies with BIP 323 by reserving version bits 5–28 for extra nonce space, thereby excluding them from soft fork signaling and suppressing warnings about unknown deployments when these bits are set in received block versions. Additional peer-to-peer improvements include updates to DNS seed handling and transport assumptions for seeded addresses. Network enhancements standardize exception monitoring between poll() and select() backends and enforce timeout intervals for peers with paused sending activity. Storage utilities have been refined by transitioning position storage to 64-bit integers within flatfiles, optimizing data management. Build processes have been adjusted to bypass the use of pipe2 on Darwin-based systems, and obsolete parameters have been removed from fuzzing input functions. Documentation updates cover new advancements such as deterministic ECDSA signatures with low-R grinding, and further clarify upgrade procedures related to the bitcoin wrapper and libexec components.
These collective improvements reflect contributions from a dedicated group of developers and translators, whose efforts continue to drive Bitcoin Core’s reliability and advancement. For further details on announcements, users can visit [this link](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/).
